description: Level-3 ruleset for Indian employment contracts. Employment is statute-heavy (Minimum Wages, EPF, Payment of Wages, Factories/Shops, Maternity, POSH, Industrial Employment Standing Orders), so much of the 'rule' logic is mandatory statutory compliance, not optional context. AI fills the features; these reviewed rules decide the document.

baseline_clauses.why: Wages — must not fall below applicable minimum wage.
baseline_clauses.legal_basis: Minimum Wages Act, 1948; Payment of Wages Act, 1936; Code on Wages, 2019

baseline_clauses.why: Duties and obligations of the employee.

baseline_clauses.legal_basis: Factories Act, 1948 / State Shops & Establishments Act

baseline_clauses.why: Statutory benefits (PF/ESI) — EPF non-deduction is a criminal offence.
baseline_clauses.legal_basis: EPF & MP Act, 1952 s.14; ESI Act, 1948

baseline_clauses.why: Assignment of work-product IP to employer.
Statutory-compliance umbrella — employer complies with all applicable labour codes.

rules.why: Post-employment non-compete — enforceable in India only if narrowly tied to confidential information.
Non-solicitation of clients and employees — independently selectable (more enforceable in India than a post-term non-compete).
rules.note: Decoupled from non-compete 2026-06-15 (closed gap G-NS); include_non_solicit derived in generationControls.

rules.why: Exclusivity / dual-employment restriction for senior roles or sensitive IP.
Garden leave during notice for senior / leadership roles.
Employee handling personal data triggers DPDP-aligned obligations.
Trade-secret-handling roles get heightened employee confidentiality.
Maternity benefits apply to female employees under the Maternity Benefit Act.
POSH policy + Internal Committee mandatory for workplaces with 10+ employees.
Senior/leadership and many startup hires have ESOPs / variable pay needing a dedicated, tax-aware clause.
rules.legal_basis: Companies Act, 2013 s.62(1)(b); SEBI SBEB Regulations, 2021

rules.why: Fixed-term employment changes term, non-renewal treatment, and grants pro-rata gratuity under the IR Code / IESO Rules 2018.
rules.legal_basis: Industrial Relations Code, 2020; IESO (Amendment) Rules, 2018; Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 s.4

rules.why: Factory employment is governed by the stricter Factories Act, 1948 hours/overtime/spread-over regime rather than the State Shops & Establishments default.
Senior/leadership hires commonly waive probation or take a short confirmation period rather than a standard probation.

fallback_policy.principle: Open-world honest degradation, but employment has a hard floor: statutory-compliance clauses (wages, EPF, working hours, gratuity) are NON-NEGOTIABLE and always included regardless of situation.
fallback_policy.when_no_rule_matches: Produce the baseline contract with all statutory clauses.
fallback_policy.review_message: This contract may involve obligations (e.g. maternity, POSH, fixed-term, ESOP) we don't yet have a specific rule for — a lawyer review is recommended.

gaps_summary: STATUTORY (highest priority): no POSH clause (G3), no maternity rule (G2), and the compliance-umbrella clause referenced in the blueprint isn't actually wired (G1). These are legal-risk gaps, not nice-to-haves.

QUICK WINS: G1 (compliance-with-law) and G4 (data-processing) reference clauses that ALREADY EXIST in the library — they just aren't wired into the employment blueprint. Add them and they work immediately; G1 is also a current compliance hole.

FORMAT VALIDATION: the ruleset format generalised to employment, but employment needed two things NDA didn't — (a) a large set of always-on STATUTORY baseline clauses with legal_basis, and (b) features tied to compliance facts (headcount, female employee, workplace type), not just commercial preferences. The format handled both; recommend adding a 'mandatory: true' marker on statutory rules so they can never be toggled off.
